name: Ugro Capital Ltd
title: Ugro Capital Ltd - 511742 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Defocus-to-focus pivot on track: disbursements record INR3,159 cr, focused book 53% of AUM, but credit cost rose to 3.6% of average on-book loans from 2.8% and AUM was flat QoQ.

triggers.quote: Credit cost was ₹86.9 crore, against ₹65.6 crore in the previous quarter, or 3.6% of average on-book loans against 2.8% earlier.

triggers.label: Focused book 32% → 53% of AUM
triggers.quote: the two focus business have risen from 32% of AUM in December 2025 to 53% today

triggers.label: Portfolio yield 18.7%, up 108 bps YoY
triggers.quote: portfolio yield now was up to 18.7%, which is up 53 basis points on the quarter and 108 basis points on the year.

triggers.label: Opex run rate in line with FY27 guidance
triggers.quote: The run rate remains in line with our FY27 guidance.

guidance.quote: we are guiding annual growth of 20% to 30% for Emerging Market LAP and 35% to 40% for GROx
Our FY29 objective is a steady-state ROA ranging between 3% to 3.5% as against 2.7% today on a pro forma basis.

guidance.metric: Focused business share of AUM FY29
guidance.quote: by FY29, both these businesses put together would be about 87% of the total portfolio

prior_guidance_check.quote: The run rate remains in line with our FY27 guidance.

red_flags.label: Credit cost up sharply QoQ
red_flags.quote: The driver is largely seasoning of our newer Emerging Market portfolio and the GROx loan portfolio.

red_flags.label: Accounting net worth cut by merger
red_flags.quote: Pro forma net worth after the scheme is about INR2,454 crores or about INR158 per share against a reported book value of INR195 a share.

red_flags.quote: every quarter should be better than the previous quarter.

evasions.topic: Profit growth in H2 vs H1
evasions.quote: Sir, my belief is that the quarter-on-quarter profit you are seeing is something we will certainly deliver.
Hopefully, if we continue this performance, sooner rather than later, it will reflect in our ratings as well.

summary.headline: UGRO Capital Q2 FY27: net disbursements up 77% YoY to INR3,159 crores, PBT INR68.3 crores (+12% YoY), with credit cost up to 3.6% of average on-book loans.
summary.overview: UGRO reported Q2 FY27 with record net disbursements of INR3,159 crores and every month above INR1,000 crores, while Emerging Market LAP and GROx rose to 53% of AUM from 32% nine months earlier. Profit before tax was INR68.3 crores (+12% YoY, +11% QoQ) and PAT was INR50.7 crores; PAT for H1 was INR118.6 crores. Credit cost rose to INR86.9 crores (3.6% of average on-book loans vs 2.8% in Q1), which management attributed to seasoning of newer EM LAP and GROx portfolios. Management also detailed the pending Profectus merger, which lowers reported net worth to a pro forma INR2,454 crores (about INR158 per share) but is expected to raise capital adequacy to about 22%; NCLT final hearing is on 20 November.

financial_highlights.value: INR86.9 crores (3.6% of average on-book loans)
10.19% on total debt of about INR10,973 crores

segments.name: Emerging Market LAP
segments.commentary: AUM INR4,268 crores (+10% QoQ, +42% YoY); disbursed INR692 crores in Q2 vs INR592 crores in Q1. Portfolio yield about 18.4%, gross NPA 2%, 317 branches across 13 states. Average monthly disbursement per branch about INR73 lakh vs INR62 lakh in Q1 and INR48 lakh in FY26.

segments.name: GROx (embedded merchant finance)
segments.commentary: AUM INR3,661 crores (+22% QoQ, up from INR1,270 crores 12 months ago). Disbursed INR2,253 crores in Q2 vs INR1,853 crores in Q1; about 750 crores per month, roughly 83,000 loans. Portfolio yield about 26%, gross NPA 1.4%, active merchants about 4.1 lakh.

segments.name: Defocused book (prime intermediated LAP, business and machinery loans)
segments.commentary: AUM fell to INR7,090 crores from INR10,458 crores nine months earlier; down 13% in Q2 alone and 32% over nine months, now 47% of AUM. Gross NPA about 3.9%.

segments.name: Co-lending and direct assignment
segments.commentary: Net income INR109.1 crores from gross income of INR160.9 crores less early-repayment reversals of INR51.8 crores (vs INR68.7 crores in Q1).

segments.name: Other income (insurance distribution, debt syndication, GROx Technologies)

guidance_outlook: FY29 objective: EM LAP plus GROx at 85% of AUM (management cited about 87% on a later answer); steady-state ROA of 3% to 3.5% (pro forma H1 FY27 ROA 2.7%, Q2 ROA 2.1%).

Growth guidance: EM LAP 20% to 30% annually (25% to 30% in a later answer); GROx 35% to 40% annually; GROx share of AUM expected to be about 25% to 30% given high repayment run-rate; EM LAP about 60% of AUM.
FY27 operating cost guidance of INR490 crores and above; Q2 run rate INR127 crores, down from INR205 crores in Q4 FY26.
Pro forma net worth after merger about INR2,454 crores (about INR158 per share); merger sanction hearing at NCLT on 20 November.
No new equity required through FY29 per management; committed to funding growth without new equity for three years.
Management stated every quarter should be better than the previous quarter on profit; post-merger H2 uplift expected from lower reversals.
Surveillance rating review expected to begin by end of calendar Q4 2026; no rating upgrade assumed yet.
capex_capacity: EM LAP network of 317 branches across 13 states; management says no new branches needed for growth; 107 mature branches (up from 81 in March) disbursing about INR86 lakh per month; 200 branches about one year old, including 138 under six months, disbursing about INR60 lakh per month.

Target average disbursement productivity of INR80 lakh to INR85 lakh per branch per month within the next few months; management said the network could disburse about INR3,300 crores a year at mature-branch productivity vs current run rate of about INR2,800 crores.
Over 1,800 sales executives and over 500 field collection officers in EM LAP.
Liquidity of about INR1,500 crores at quarter-end; new long-term borrowings of about INR1,045 crores raised in the quarter; about 68% of borrowings have run beyond three years.
demand_pricing: Monthly disbursements above INR1,000 crores in each month: INR1,057 crores in July, INR1,010 crores in August, INR1,092 crores in September.
Management expects the defocused book to keep running down, so total AUM growth is slower than disbursement growth.
Floating-rate share of borrowings about 50%; about 45% of borrowings from banks on one-year MCLR resets; management expects 15 to 20 bps impact on longer-term loans from recent rate hikes.
Loans against property are floating-rate; GROx and remaining prime unsecured loans are fixed; loan-book reset around three months (URR-linked) per management.
GROx partners provide default loss guarantees within RBI limits; collection-linked payouts of 5% to 7% tied to partner portfolio performance.

qa_highlights.question: What will the focused vs defocused AUM split be in two years, and what provision coverage is needed as GROx grows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said focused businesses were 32% of AUM at the strategic reset and are 53% now, with about 87% targeted by FY29. Coverage is 45% overall; GROx coverage goes up to 70% to 75% but GROx is a small-ticket book with write-offs after a lag, and its net AUM contribution will be modest given high repayments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of shareholder overhang from strategic investors, and what risks exist in the GROx book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IFU (15.5%) and ADV (about 9.5%) remain long-term strategic holders and Samena has stepped off the Board; overhang from public holders will take time to clear given the share price correction. On GROx, management cited about 25 months of operations and two full credit cycles, with risk mitigated by reducing partner and geographic concentration.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the rate environment on cost of borrowing, and when could ratings improve?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of borrowings are floating; cost of borrowing rose about 5 bps QoQ to 10.19%. Management said liquidity is ample and rating agencies are engaged; the annual surveillance is expected to begin by end-calendar Q4 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How much will H2 profit grow relative to H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said every quarter should be better than the previous quarter, citing run-down of low-yield book, full-year benefit of higher-yield portfolio, and no added overhead; the merger should add further benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Will the income recognition change affect gross revenue or profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said past co-lending and assignment income is adjusted once against reserves with no P&L charge; future co-lending/assignment income will be lower on the behavioral tenure basis, while interest income is unchanged. Clarified that the impact is recorded as gain on derecognition of financial instruments, not other income.

risks_watch: Credit cost rose to 3.6% of average on-book loans from 2.8%, driven by seasoning of new EM LAP and GROx portfolios; management flagged this as the line to monitor most closely.
Pro forma net worth falls to about INR2,454 crores from reported INR3,029 crores; NCLT sanction (hearing 20 November) and statutory auditor review are pending.
Market value of about INR1,130 crores (about 0.4x reported book value) at end-October; management attributes this to past volatility and expects execution to re-rate the stock.
Rate risk: about 45% of borrowings reset on one-year MCLR; management expects 15 to 20 bps impact on longer-term loans; cost of borrowing already up about 5 bps QoQ.
GROx is unsecured and short-tenure, with partner concentration and geographic concentration noted as risks; management said diversification is in progress.
Management's H2 profit outlook is qualitative ('every quarter better than the previous quarter') rather than numeric.
key_quotes: For the first time in our history, UGRO disbursed more than INR1,000 crores in every single month of the quarter; INR1,057 crores in July, INR1,010 crores in August and INR1,092 crores in September.

The credit cost, as a percentage of average AUM, is about 2% for the half year. It remains well within the lifetime expected losses on the portfolio that we underwrite. And this is the line item, which we will be monitoring more closely in the coming quarters.
So, from a profit guidance perspective, every quarter should be better than the previous quarter.
I believe the most effective answer management can give on valuation is execution, and that remains our approach.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the operating pivot: disbursement volumes, branch productivity, and the claim that every quarter's profit will beat the prior one. Cautious and evasive on valuation (market value about 0.4x book, answered only with "execution") and on the H2 profit path, which is qualitative rather than numeric. Management also stressed that the credit cost rise is the line item to monitor.

adds.what: EM LAP branches: 200 branches about one year old (138 under six months) ramping; no new branches needed per management

growth.why: Management guides EM LAP AUM growth of 20-30% and GROx 35-40% annually, backed by a 317-branch network already in place (target productivity INR80-85 lakh/branch/month vs ~INR73 lakh now) and GROx disbursements of ~INR750 crores/month, though no new capacity capex is planned and the defocused book is running down.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says every quarter should beat the prior one on profit; PPOP rose 22% QoQ to INR155.1 crores and opex fell to INR127.2 crores vs INR205 crores in Q4 FY26, though credit cost rose to 3.6% from 2.8%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management says no new branches are needed; 317 branches in 13 states, with 200 branches under one year old, can disburse about INR3,300 crores a year at mature productivity vs about INR2,800 crores run rate.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Guidance is EM LAP AUM growth of 20-30% and GROx 35-40% a year; net disbursements hit INR3,159 crores (+77% YoY) with every month above INR1,000 crores, though total AUM was flat QoQ at INR15,019 crores as the defocused book runs down 13% in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Branch network is already in place and management says no new branches are needed; no capex plan was discussed, and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided qualitatively that every quarter will beat the last, with no numeric guidance; a rating upgrade is not assumed until the surveillance review starting by end-calendar Q4 2026.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit cost rose to INR86.9 crores (3.6% of average on-book loans vs 2.8% in Q1) from seasoning of EM LAP and GROx books, and about 45% of borrowings reset on one-year MCLR with 15-20 bps impact expected; the NCLT hearing on 20 November could also move the pro forma net worth.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch was discussed; the focus is EM LAP and GROx.

rows.label: Profectus merger and NCLT sanction
rows.why: Pro forma net worth falls to INR2,454 crores (about INR158 per share) from reported INR3,029 crores, but capital adequacy is expected to rise to about 22% from 18.8%.

rows.label: No new equity through FY29
rows.why: Management says growth will be funded without new equity for three years, with liquidity of about INR1,500 crores and leverage at 3.6x.

rows.label: Surveillance rating review
rows.why: Surveillance review is expected to start by end of calendar Q4 2026, with no upgrade assumed yet, and cost of borrowing is already up about 5 bps QoQ to 10.19%.

tone.note: Management was confident on disbursement volumes, branch productivity and the profit trajectory, and cautious on the 3.6% credit cost and valuation at about 0.4x book; analysts pressed on H2 profit quantum, GROx credit risk, shareholder overhang and rate impact on borrowing costs.
